The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ is given above. Find ${f}^{′}(1.5).$

${f}^{′}(1.5)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
To compute ${f}^{′}(1.5),$ we need to find the slope of the tangent to $f(x)$ at $x=1.5.$

Let's consider the graph of $y=f(x)$ for $x\in [-1,3].$ Notice that $x=1.5$ lies in this interval.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934289/assets/56cb6eb057efc5bf73e92fea0a78bacdf4bdd1ac43fdd28b23b08bbbbdff346c.png)

The slope of $y=f(x)$ on $x\in (-1,3)$ is constant and equals

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δx} & =\frac{0-2}{3-(-1)}=\frac{-2}{4}=-0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(1.5)=-0.5.$
